root_cause.text: `nft_dynset_expr_setup()` in the nf_tables dynset path did not clean up already-cloned stateful set element expressions when cloning a later expression failed, so the earlier cloned expression remained allocated and leaked on the error path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `nft_dynset_expr_setup()` to jump to `err_out` and call `nft_set_elem_expr_destroy(&ctx, elem_expr)` when `nft_expr_clone(..., GFP_ATOMIC)` fails, and the CVE text explicitly says “If cloning the second stateful expression in the element via GFP_ATOMIC fails, then the first stateful expression remains in place without being released.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a public declaration for the set element expression destruction helper so it can be used for cleanup.
intent_record.what: A new function prototype, `void nft_set_elem_expr_destroy(const struct nft_ctx *ctx, struct nft_set_elem_expr *elem_expr);`, was added to the header alongside the existing `nft_set_elem_expr_clone()` declaration.
intent_record.how: This exposes a destroy/cleanup routine for set element expressions to other translation units, enabling callers to explicitly release expression resources that were previously not declared here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Export `nft_set_elem_expr_destroy()` so it can be used outside its defining file.
intent_record.what: The function declaration for `nft_set_elem_expr_destroy()` was changed from `static void` to non-static `void`, making the symbol globally visible instead of file-local. The function body and parameters remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This change allows other translation units to call `nft_set_elem_expr_destroy()`, whereas before it was only usable within the defining source file. Runtime behavior of the function itself does not change; only its linkage and external accessibility do.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix dynset expression setup to clean up partially constructed element expressions when cloning fails.
intent_record.what: The function `nft_dynset_expr_setup()` now initializes a local `struct nft_ctx ctx` with the set's network namespace and table family, changes the clone-failure path from an immediate `return -1` to `goto err_out`, and adds an `err_out` label that calls `nft_set_elem_expr_destroy(&ctx, elem_expr)` before returning `-1`.
intent_record.how: On clone failure, the partially built element expression is now explicitly cleaned up instead of being left allocated, preventing resource leakage and ensuring the setup path unwinds correctly when expression cloning does not complete.

Sven Auhagen reports transaction failures with following error:
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit fa23e0d4b756d25829e124d6b670a4c6bbd4bf7e
Author: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Date:   Wed May 8 14:52:47 2024 +0200

    netfilter: nf_tables: allow clone callbacks to sleep
    
    Sven Auhagen reports transaction failures with following error:
      ./main.nft:13:1-26: Error: Could not process rule: Cannot allocate memory
      percpu: allocation failed, size=16 align=8 atomic=1, atomic alloc failed, no space left
    
    This points to failing pcpu allocation with GFP_ATOMIC flag.
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the exact vulnerable pattern in `nft_dynset_expr_setup()`: inside the loop, it clones each expression with `nft_expr_clone(expr, priv->expr_array[i], GFP_ATOMIC)` and immediately returns `-1` on failure: `if (nft_expr_clone(...) < 0) return -1;`. The root cause says that when cloning a later expression fails, already-cloned stateful set element expressions are not cleaned up, causing a leak. This function body still has the early-return-on-failure path and shows no cleanup of previously cloned expressions before returning. The commit shown only changes the GFP flag to `GFP_ATOMIC`; it does not add any error-path cleanup, so the fix for the leak is not present here.

This patch replaces NFT_SET_EXPR by NF
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 563125a73ac30d7036ae69ca35c40500562c1de4
Author: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
Date:   Wed Dec 9 20:10:27 2020 +0100

    netfilter: nftables: generalize set extension to support for several expressions
    
    This patch replaces NFT_SET_EXPR by NFT_SET_EXT_EXPRESSIONS. This new
    extension allows to attach several expressions to one set element (not
    only one single expression as NFT_SET_EXPR provides). This patch
    prepares for support for several expressions per set
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet. The relevant setup helper here is `nft_dynset_expr_setup()`, which clones multiple expressions in a loop: `for (i = 0; i < priv->num_exprs; i++) { ... if (nft_expr_clone(expr, priv->expr_array[i]) < 0) return -1; ... }`. In this commit version, the caller `nft_dynset_init()` already cleans up all previously allocated expressions on the error path: `err_expr_free: for (i = 0; i < priv->num_exprs; i++) nft_expr_destroy(ctx, priv->expr_array[i]);`. That means the earlier cloned expression is not leaked if a later clone/setup step fails. Also, the old single-expression path `priv->expr != NULL && nft_expr_clone(...) < 0` has been replaced by the multi-expression array handling, so the exact buggy construct from the root cause is absent. Therefore `has_bug` is false and the fix is already present.
